stem: A screening program contacts everyone with a positive result. Before confirmatory testing, the program wants to estimate the fraction of these people who actually have the condition. Which of the following quantities answers that question?

options.label: A
options.text: True positive results divided by all positive results
options.explanation: Positive predictive value uses the positive-test group as its denominator. It describes the fraction of those positive results that represent actual disease, which is the program’s question.
options.misconception: No misconception: PPV counts true positives among all positive results.

options.label: B
options.text: True cases detected divided by all people with disease
options.explanation: This describes sensitivity, the fraction of actual cases the screening test detects. It starts with people known to have disease, rather than the group contacted after positive results.
options.misconception: Confuses detection among actual cases with disease among positive results.

options.label: C
options.text: True negatives divided by all people without disease
options.explanation: This describes specificity, the fraction of disease-free people correctly testing negative. It does not estimate the fraction of positive results that correspond to actual disease.
options.misconception: Substitutes disease-free negative classification for positive predictive value.

options.label: D
options.text: False positive results divided by people without disease
options.explanation: This describes false-positive results among people without disease. The requested quantity instead starts with everyone testing positive and asks how many of them truly have disease.
options.misconception: Uses false positives among noncases instead of true disease among positives.

options.label: E
options.text: All people with disease divided by everyone screened
options.explanation: This describes disease frequency in the screened population. Positive predictive value instead restricts the denominator to positive results, rather than including everyone who was screened.
options.misconception: Substitutes whole-population disease frequency for the positive-test fraction.

context:
Learning objective: Choose the positive-test denominator for positive predictive value before applying it to a screening table.

Positive predictive value uses the positive-test group as its denominator. It describes the fraction of those positive results that represent actual disease, which is the program’s question.
